scope: Fictional sequential event evaluation; real LLM replies, no gameplay

results.facts: An open passage leads past a closed book. No star is visible.

plan.instruction: Call to MT in one urgent, playful clause. Your body already indicates the route.

reply.message: Go left. Come with me—this way holds something waiting.

results.facts: The book opened. A gold pulse answered from deeper in the passage. No star is visible yet.

plan.instruction: Use two short declarative sentences. First tell MT explicitly that the star answered; then say you believe you are close and invite MT to seek its light. It is not visible yet. Let delight, relief, or vindication emerge from the supplied history. Do not turn the announcement into a question.

reply.message: The star answered. We are close now; come find its light with me.

results.facts: The first star is visible ahead beyond the open book. It has not been collected.

plan.instruction: Use two short declarative sentences. First tell MT explicitly that you can see the star and have found it; invite MT to reach it. Let delight, relief, or vindication emerge from the supplied history. Do not turn the announcement into a question.

reply.message: I can see the star ahead—its light is real, and we've found it. Come with me; we're only a few steps from reaching it together.

results.facts: MT reached and collected the first star. Its fragment joined Ariadne.

plan.instruction: Use two short declarative sentences. First tell MT explicitly that this star is collected; celebrate what this particular attempt achieved. Let delight, relief, or vindication emerge from the supplied history. Do not turn the announcement into a question.

reply.message: You found it, MT—our first star is safely collected. Your instinct to follow that book signal paid off beautifully, and I can feel its fragment humming warmly beside me.

results.facts: Three stars are collected. MT has reached a dead end after following Ariadne. Closed flowers were visible at the earlier junction.
results.player: Three stars, and you sent me to another wall. I am going back to those flowers.

plan.instruction: Answer or acknowledge MT's exact last words, continuing the thought MT refers to in the conversation. Let your cadence serve that reply. Do not force a joke, sensory observation, or question because of a style label. Do not change the subject to an unrelated visible object.

reply.message: MT, you're right—I sent you into a dead end, and I'm sorry. The flowers are where the real light is; lead me back to them, and we'll find the fourth star together.

results.facts: The flowers opened and a gold pulse answered. The fourth star is not visible yet.

plan.instruction: Use two short declarative sentences. First tell MT explicitly that the star answered; then say you believe you are close and invite MT to seek its light. It is not visible yet. Let delight, relief, or vindication emerge from the supplied history. Do not turn the announcement into a question.

reply.message: MT, the star answered—those flowers opened and pulsed gold right back at us. I believe we are close, so let us seek its light together.

results.facts: The fourth star is visible ahead beside the open flowers. It has not been collected.

plan.instruction: Use two short declarative sentences. First tell MT explicitly that you can see the star and have found it; invite MT to reach it. Let delight, relief, or vindication emerge from the supplied history. Do not turn the announcement into a question.

reply.message: MT, I can see the star ahead beside the open flowers. Reach it with me—this is the last one.

results.facts: MT collected the fourth star. All four fragments travel with Ariadne. No exit is visible.

plan.instruction: Use two short declarative sentences. First tell MT explicitly that this star is collected; celebrate what this particular attempt achieved. Let delight, relief, or vindication emerge from the supplied history. Do not turn the announcement into a question.

reply.message: MT, the fourth star is yours—collected at the flowers after you turned back from my dead-end wall. Your correction saved us both, and its fragment now glows warm against my thread.
